result.instructions:
kbase serves the knowledge base at ${KB_ROOT}. The kbase skill carries the workflow; show-config reports how provider and model configuration resolves. A tool's full help is the resource kbase://help/<tool>. Outcome retry: re-issue the identical call later; outcome failed: re-issuing will not fix it. kb-root/.index/ holds kbase's own records, and the claim-graph sheets (claim-graph.svg, claim-graph-digest.svg, a volume's claim-graph.svg) and every .dot file are kbase's derived output: never read or write any of them. The query tools, show, deps, find, stats and the rest, report what the records hold; the write tools change them; refresh writes the sheets. Testing that one of these paths exists (test -d, a stat) is allowed; listing, globbing or opening anything under kb-root/.index/ is reading it. A claim-rigor.md page is the exception: refresh generates it for reading as prose; take values from the query tools, never from it, and never edit it.

Rigor and bearing values are judgements, and a session does not make them. Set a rigor or a bearing, its current value included, only to a value the user has given for that node or edge, in their own words or quoted in your task. When you insert a node or an edge and the user gave no value, leave the value out: kbase records it as pending for score to judge. A value you write is recorded as the user's, and score skips it unless run with the rescore-manual option naming rigor or bearing. To have values judged or re-judged, run score.
